transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Recording: https://redwood-recordings/fireflies/ff-20270830-riverview-001
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood CSM), Dana Morris (CTO, Riverview), Sam Patel (Lead DevOps), Lena Ortiz (Product Ops), Jamal Greene (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff to align on onboarding scope, security checklist, infra access, and pilot success criteria.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh yeah this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE working with Riverview, with me is priya, our se, miguel from success and we'll run through a quick agenda, sound good?
[00:12] Dana Morris: yep, thanks alex, really appreciate it, excited to get started. we, uh, want to make sure this goes smoothly - we have a couple of regulatory constraints and some tight latency SLAs for our triage product.
[00:25] Priya Kapoor: great, quick agenda, we'll cover the onboarding playbook, deployment options (hosted / dedicated / private), security/compliance touchpoints, networking steps for VPC peering or private deploy, and then pilot success metrics and timelines. we'll leave time for q&a.
[00:40] Sam Patel: just to flag, from infra side we prefer private or dedicated if possible because of data residency and audit requirements, but we need to understand the cost delta.
[00:52] Alex Chen: totally we see that a lot - we'll map the tradeoffs. just quick housekeeping, i'll send the deck and onboarding playbook after the call.
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: okay starting with deployment options: hosted api is fastest to get started, low friction - you hit our hosted endpoints, tokens encrypted in transit and at rest, but for audit and residency you may prefer dedicated capacity or our private deployment. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, private gives you a customer-managed control plane and VPC/on-prem option.
[01:35] Dana Morris: can you quantify the latency difference? our SLAs are 200ms p95 for short completions, and some calls will be longer.
[01:45] Priya Kapoor: short answers - hosted on nearest region typically best latency baseline; dedicated with colocated pools can get similar p95 if pinned; private depends on your network config but gives lower data egress risk. tradeoffs: hosted is easiest, dedicated gives throughput & isolation, private gives full control and residency. also note that our runtime picks kernels and batching strategies - if you need low tail latency we recommend small batch sizes + prefix caching enabled.
[02:18] Jamal Greene: on security side we need SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO integration, and KMS/HSM for key management. also audit logs for every request and retention policy controls.
[02:30] Miguel Torres: yep we've got a security pack - i'll share SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and you can integrate with customer KMS for private deployments. audit logs are available via the console and can be exported.
[02:45] Sam Patel: is there a standard template for the VPC peering? firewall and route table requirements?
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: yes, we'll provide a network spec doc - open ports are minimal, mostly outbound to our control plane for private deploy; for dedicated you typically set up secure tunnel or peering. i'll share the exact CIDR and ports in the architecture doc.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: what's the usual timeline for going from kickoff to pilot? we have a Q4 go-live target.
[03:18] Alex Chen: typical onboarding is 4-8 weeks for a pilot depending on infra readiness. if you go hosted you can often run a pilot in 1-2 weeks; dedicated/private adds time for network and compliance checks so plan 4-8 weeks. Q4 target seems doable if infra access and stakeholders are confirmed in next week or two.
[03:45] Dana Morris: good. our success criteria: 1) p95 latency under 250ms for 90% of triage queries, 2) cost under $X per 1k tokens (we'll share numbers offline), 3) SOC2-compliant audit logs and KMS integration.
[04:05] Priya Kapoor: perfect, we'll document those in the pilot SOW. for cost we usually recommend quantization profiles and batching strategies, plus caching for prefix reuse - redwood optimize will suggest config. note - transcription sometimes has product name mixups but 'Redwood Optimize' is our cost/performance toolkit.
[04:25] Sam Patel: any benchmarks for your verified models? we saw a spreadsheet in the repo but want something representative of our workloads (mostly short prompts).
[04:34] Priya Kapoor: we'll run a small benchmark using your sample prompt set - you'll provide the prompt pack and expected distribution, and we can run with hosted or dedicated instances to compare latency and cost. i'll include recommended quantization (e.g., 4-bit int8 like q4f, depending on model) - apologies, i sometimes say q4f, i mean q4_0 variant - there are a lot of names.
[04:58] Dana Morris: sounds good. for compliance, we may need an on-prem option for a subset of traffic - is that supported?
[05:06] Miguel Torres: yes, private deployment supports on-prem packaged install and VPC deployments. we'll coordinate with your security team to review the checklist.
[05:15] Jamal Greene: do you provide HSM integrations? we use an HSM for key custody for a few services.
[05:21] Priya Kapoor: yes for private deployments you can integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and manage keys, but enterprise customers can bring their own KMS for an additional configuration.
[05:35] Sam Patel: how do rollouts work? if we pin a model version, can we do canaries?
[05:40] Alex Chen: yes, redwood supports rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies; console provides per-route dashboards and tracing hooks so you can monitor regressions.
[05:52] Lena Ortiz: action items, who owns what?
[06:00] Alex Chen: i'll take onboarding playbook and pricing, priya will do architecture and bench plan, miguel will handle success plan and the SOW, sam you'll provide infra access details, jamal will send security questions.
[06:12] Dana Morris: that works. couple of Qs from my side - retention: can we set data retention windows per environment?
[06:20] Priya Kapoor: yes retention policies are configurable per deployment; for hosted we have retention controls and you can request longer retention for audit reasons. for private you control retention entirely.
[06:35] Sam Patel: network specifics - do you require outbound to any specific endpoints for hosted?
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: hosted is just standard TLS outbound to api.redwood.ai endpoints, ports 443. we'll send IP ranges if you prefer IP whitelisting.
[06:50] Jamal Greene: for audit and logging - are logs structured and exportable to our SIEM?
[06:55] Miguel Torres: yep audit logs are JSON structured, we can stream them to your SIEM or you can pull via the console.
[07:05] Dana Morris: one more, pricing - how do we estimate cost for dedicated nodes?
[07:10] Alex Chen: dedicated is commit-based monthly pricing; we'll send a pricing sheet with examples tied to throughput, tokens/sec, and GPU types. we'll also include Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce per-token cost.
[07:25] Priya Kapoor: ok quick walk-through of initial pilot scope: 1) pilot uses 2 routes - triage short prompts and longer summarization; 2) we will evaluate on latency, cost, and correctness against your test set; 3) plan to run bench on hosted and dedicated variants to compare.
[07:48] Sam Patel: for the bench we can provide 10k sample prompts and expected labels; what's the best format?
[07:54] Priya Kapoor: newline-delimited JSON with metadata is ideal, we'll provide a template in the playbook.
[08:05] Lena Ortiz: stakeholders - i'll confirm product ops and legal.
[08:10] Dana Morris: i'll loop in procurement for contracts.
[08:15] Alex Chen: perfect, next steps recap: alex sends playbook & pricing by sept 1, priya sends arch + bench plan by sept 3, sam shares infra details by sept 7, jamal to send security Qs by sept 2.
[08:30] Miguel Torres: i'll prep the SOW draft once we have the bench scope.
[08:38] Dana Morris: any gotchas for data residency in europe vs us? we mostly host in us but want options for future.
[08:46] Priya Kapoor: we support region pinning and can deploy in eu regions for private/dedicated if needed; we'll include region costs in the sheet.
[08:58] Sam Patel: small nit - we've seen model names get mangled in docs, e.g., 'red wood console' - just want canonical names in the playbook please.
[09:05] Alex Chen: noted, we'll keep canonical product names and version numbers.
[09:15] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, i'm feeling good about this plan.
[09:20] Alex Chen: great, one final thing - any preference on weekly pilot sync cadence?
[09:25] Dana Morris: weekly for first two weeks, then biweekly.
[09:30] Miguel Torres: i'll send calendar invites after the call.
[09:35] Alex Chen: awesome, thanks all. we'll follow up via email with links to docs.
[09:40] Dana Morris: thanks, bye.
